ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the lower-left part of the figure is a cyclohexadienone skeleton; the carbonyl O in the upper left is visible, and there are two C=C double bonds in the ring; the right side is connected to a saturated three-membered ring/cyclopropane part, and bears an upper methyl and a lower-right alkyl substituent. The figure also has curved arrows and position labels such as α, β, δ, etc.; according to the problem statement, these are not written into the SMILES as atoms or bonds. Reasoning: After ignoring the curved arrows and non-atom labels, only the heavy-atom skeleton is retained. According to the specified method, writing starts from the terminal carbon of the ethyl substituent on the lower-right cyclopropane carbon, giving `CCC1`. Next, proceed along the saturated three-membered ring to the adjacent upper carbon, and write the methyl on that carbon as a branch `C(C)`. Then go to the shared bridgehead/connection carbon, close the three-membered ring with the number `1`, and at the same time open the cyclohexadienone ring with the number `2`, giving `C12`. Finally, write along the six-membered cyclohexadienone part as `C=CC=CC2=O`. Splicing the parts together gives `CCC1C(C)C12C=CC=CC2=O`.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: Redraw the heavy-atom graph from the image after removing the curved arrows and non-atom labels. Start the SMILES at the terminal carbon of the ethyl substituent on the lower/right cyclopropane carbon, giving `CCC1`. Move around the saturated three-membered ring to the adjacent upper carbon and add its methyl branch as `C(C)`. Then go to the shared junction carbon, close the cyclopropane with digit `1`, and open the cyclohexadienone ring with digit `2`, giving `C12`. Finally traverse the six-membered cyclohexadienone portion as `C=CC=CC2=O`. Concatenating these pieces yields `CCC1C(C)C12C=CC=CC2=O`.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中下方偏左是一个环己二烯酮骨架，可见左上方的羰基 O，环内有两个 C=C 双键；右侧连着一个饱和三元环/环丙烷部分，并带有上方甲基和右下方烷基取代。图中还有弯曲箭头以及 α、β、δ 等位置标注，这些按题意不作为原子或键来写入 SMILES。
推理：忽略弯曲箭头和非原子标注后，只保留重原子骨架。按指定方法，从右下方环丙烷碳上的乙基取代基末端碳开始书写，得到 `CCC1`。接着沿饱和三元环到相邻上方碳，并把该碳上的甲基作为支链写成 `C(C)`。再到共享的桥头/连接碳，用数字 `1` 闭合三元环，同时用数字 `2` 开启环己二烯酮环，得到 `C12`。最后沿六元环己二烯酮部分书写为 `C=CC=CC2=O`。拼接各部分得到 `CCC1C(C)C12C=CC=CC2=O`。

The curved mechanistic arrows and Greek labels are ignored; hydrogens are treated implicitly in the SMILES.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply skeletal-structure conventions, implicit hydrogens, SMILES branch notation, ring-closure numbering, and bond-order notation. Encode the ketone as `C=O`, the two alkene bonds as `C=C`, the methyl branch as `(C)`, and use ring digits to close the cyclopropane and cyclohexadienone rings.
